tier_reason: Slide 'Performance in Node (native, preliminary)' in the NodeConf EU 2023 deck shows autocannon output for llhttp (avg 28,808 req/s, 317k req in 11.02s) and milo (avg 30,765.1 req/s, 338k req in 11.02s). These are first-party numbers from a single run with no CPU, compiler, flags or harness code given. The repo's benchmarks/cpp and benchmarks/wasm harnesses against llhttp state flags but publish no numbers or CPU model, so the entry stays at C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: milo avg 30,765.1 req/s (338k requests in 11.02s) vs llhttp avg 28,808 req/s (317k requests in 11.02s): about 1.07x (derived from page data). The same deck says: "Milo matches or outperforms llhttp in native mode, but it is slower when compiled in WebAssembly."
corrections.caveats: The numbers come from Paolo Insogna's NodeConf EU 2023 talk deck (Nov 2023; linked from the README as [slides] https://talks.paoloinsogna.dev/milo), not from the repo. The deck pastes autocannon text from a slide labelled "Performance in Node (native, preliminary)": one run of 11 samples, with no CPU model, compiler or flags, and no public harness for this Node native-addon test. The speedup of about 1.07x is small and sits within about 1.4 stdev of the llhttp run. The numbers predate nearly 3 years of parser changes. The same deck admits milo is slower than llhttp when compiled to WebAssembly, and WASM is the build that undici and Node use. The repo does have comparative harnesses: benchmarks/cpp (milo with RUSTFLAGS=-C target-cpu=native vs llhttp release/v9.3.1 built with clang -O3 -DNDEBUG -march=native -flto) and benchmarks/wasm (vs undici llhttp_simd.wasm). It publishes no results from them, and its benchmarks README calls them "comparative smoke tests, not absolute performance claims".
